rounds.text: Tulive Developers Ltd trades at an aggressive price-to-book multiple of 5.56x despite a complete destruction of fundamental capital efficiency [E1]. Both return on capital employed and return on equity sit deeply negative at -2.5%, proving that the underlying business operations destroy value rather than generate returns for shareholders [E5, E6]. This fundamental weakness is further underscored by a severe 5-year compounded profit contraction of -21% [E7]. Market expectations have entirely detached from operational reality, with recent price growth outpacing profit growth by 15% and signalling that expectations are running well ahead of delivery [E34]. Compounding this disconnect, the screen flags clear earnings growth deceleration [E47], while income-seeking investors receive zero support given a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: the stock has demonstrated strong historical momentum through a 1-year share price growth of 28%, 3-year growth of 87%, 5-year growth of 47%, and positioning near the upper boundary of its 52-week range [E4, E10, E11, E12].

Conceded: [E1], [E5], [E6], [E7], [E34], and [E47]. While backward-looking metrics and negative return ratios appear challenging, the market is aggressively forward-pricing a structural inflection rather than static accounting history, which is confirmed by the stock sitting 86% of the way up its 52-week range [E4]. This repricing is fundamentally anchored in a powerful operational turnaround where trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth has rebounded positively to 13% [E8]. Far from a temporary blip, this accelerating momentum is validated by sustained, multi-year compounding in shareholder value, including a 28% gain over 1 year, an 87% surge over 3 years, a 47% expansion over 5 years, and a robust 21% compounded share price growth over 10 years [E9, E10, E11, E12].

Conceded: [E9], [E10], [E11], and [E12]. While the bull points to multi-year share price growth of 21% to 87% to justify an aggressive re-pricing [E9, E10, E11, E12], this market enthusiasm completely detaches from the company's underlying fundamentals where ROCE and ROE are both negative at -2.5% [E5, E6]. The bull leans on a stock price sitting 86% of the way up its 52-week range [E4] and a TTM profit growth rebound of 13% [E8], but ignores that long-term compounded profit growth over 5 years sits at a devastating -21% [E7]. This divergence is precisely why the scanX signal engine flags that price growth exceeds profit growth by 15%, confirming that expectations are running far ahead of actual delivery [E34]. Furthermore, the bull's narrative of a structural inflection is directly contradicted by the screen reason warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E47]. Paying a steep 5.56x price-to-book multiple for a company with negative returns [E1, E5, E6] that offers a zero dividend yield [E3] exposes investors to severe downside when momentum fades.
